chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, altogether from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Malik ibn Atiyya, from Abu Hamza Al-Thumali, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

There is no servant who says, when it is morning before the emergence of the sun, 'Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest of all, and Glory be to Allah morning and evening, and the abundant Praise is for Allah, Lord of the worlds. There is no associate for Him, and may Allah send blessings upon Muhammad and his Progeny,' except that an Angel would initiate and make these to be in the middle of his wings, and ascend with these to the sky of the world.

So the Angels would be saying: 'What is with you?' So he would be Saying: 'With me are words which were spoke by a man from the believers, and these are such and such'. So they would be saying: 'May Allah have Mercy on the one who said these words, and Forgive (his sins) for him'.

He said: 'And every time he passes by a sky, he would say similar to that to its inhabitants, so they would be saying: 'May Allah have Mercy on the one who said these words, and Forgive (his sins) for him', until he would end up with these to the Bearers of the Throne.

So he would be saying to them: 'With me are words which were spoke by a man from the believers, and these are such and such'. So they would be saying: 'May Allah have Mercy on this servant, and Forgive (his sins) for him. Go with these to the guardians of the treasures of the speeches of the believers, for these words are the treasure, until they write these down in the Register of the Treasures'.

key_terms.كُنُوزُ مَقَالَةِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Treasures of the speeches of the believers

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for reciting morning dhikr before sunrise?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni narrates this chain from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to highlight the cosmic significance of morning dhikr, where an angel ascends through the seven heavens carrying the reciter's words. This celestial journey culminates in the 'Register of Treasures' (Diwan al-Kunuz), emphasizing that these specific phrases are considered precious spiritual assets. The hadith underscores the Shia belief in the tangible, recorded reward of daily devotions, linking earthly worship directly to heavenly validation.
